title: Live-enablement gating & environment separation
body:
## Context
R4 exists to produce **assurance, not features** (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §8). E44 is the epic that makes the live/demo boundary *structural* rather than conventional: environment becomes a typed, validated configuration axis (M1 config, `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §16.1 `ExchangeConfig.environment`), it selects credentials, hosts and storage namespaces, and a master feature flag (`trading.live_enabled` / internal registry key `live_trading`, `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §16.2) defaults OFF and cannot be turned on until the four-item Live-enablement gate in `docs/plan/07-release-and-prr.md` §6 is satisfied with recorded evidence.

Everything that can go wrong here is expensive: a demo credential reaching a live route, a live order sent from a session the user believed was demo, a manager promoted to live without an audited grant, or a deployment booting with a key that still carries withdrawal permission. E44 turns each of those from "we were careful" into "the system refuses".

Plan references:
- `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §3 (epic register, E44 = R4, `area/oms-execution`, modules M1/M14/M17, domains PAPER+ADMIN, 42 pts), §8.2-§8.3 (R4 scope and exit criteria 2 and 4).
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` §21 PAPER (US-PAPER-002, US-PAPER-003, US-PAPER-007) and §26 ADMIN (US-ADMIN-007, US-ADMIN-010, US-ADMIN-012).
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-010, SCR-074, SCR-075, SCR-122, SCR-137, SCR-145.
- `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `POST /session/environment`, `PUT /admin/feature-flags/{flagKey}`, `GET /admin/feature-flags`, `GET /admin/security/summary`.
- `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §auth_ok (`allowed_environments`), `system` topic (`SystemUpdate`, feature-flag + kill-switch broadcast).
- `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3 `exchange_accounts.env` / `exchange_env` enum / trigger `trg_ea_env_parent`, `trade_groups.tg_paper_env`.
- `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §1 `Environment`/`ExecutionMode`, §14 authorization 4-tuple, §16.1 config validation, §16.2 flag registry, §16.3 admin knob map.
- `docs/plan/07-release-and-prr.md` §6 Live-enablement gate.


### Points reconciliation (register 42 vs epic estimate 75)
The §3 epic-register figure for E44 (**42 pts**) is an **engineering-only** budget: it counts Story / Task / Spike tickets (`S`, `T`, `K`) — the code-bearing work that consumes the R4 delivery-capacity line in `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §3.1. The epic ticket's `estimate` field is, per `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md`, the **sum of all children**, which additionally includes the design (`D`), QA (`Q`) and security (`X`) tickets that are staffed from the design / QA / security disciplines rather than from the engineering capacity line.

| Bucket | Tickets | Pts |
|---|---|---|
| Engineering (S/T/K) — comparable to the register's 42 | K01, T01–T06, S01–S04 | **45** |
| Design (D) | D01–D04 | 11 |
| QA / test (Q) | Q01–Q03 | 13 |
| Security / compliance (X) | X01, X02 | 6 |
| **Epic `estimate` (sum of children)** | | **75** |

Engineering total **45** vs register **42** = **+7.1%**, inside the ±15% DoR tolerance. This is the same convention every other epic backlog file follows (e.g. E05 register 38 / epic 78, E11 register 89 / epic 154), so **no roadmap correction is required** — only an explanatory footnote, which E44-T06 adds to `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §3 so the convention is stated once for all epics rather than re-derived per file.

## Scope / Deliverables
**In scope**
- Environment as a first-class typed setting (`live` | `demo` | `testnet`) resolved once at boot from `ExchangeConfig`, with an `environment_allowlist` that excludes `testnet` from user-selectable trading (E44-T01).
- Physical storage separation for OMS-owned mutable state: a Postgres schema per environment and a QuestDB namespace per environment, with no shared mutable row reachable across environments (E44-T02).
- One middleware-level cross-environment guard on every trading route, returning `403` and a high-severity audit event, plus the trade-group mixed-environment invariant (E44-T03).
- `trading.live_enabled` master gate: flag registry entry, special-cased `PUT /admin/feature-flags/{flagKey}` requiring `reason` + `evidence_url`, gate-status computation feeding `GET /admin/security/summary` (E44-T04).
- Key-permission audit CLI/job that prints Bybit-*reported* scopes for every configured key and blocks boot in `live` when an assertion fails (E44-T01, E44-T05).
- UI: live-enablement gate surface on SCR-145 + SCR-137 (E44-S01), the hardened Demo→Live switch SCR-074 (E44-S02), the pervasive live visual language SCR-010/SCR-075 with confirm-on-every-order defaulting ON in live (E44-S03), and per-manager live eligibility on SCR-122 (E44-S04).
- ADR-0016 recording the environment-separation decision (E44-T06).
- Design (E44-D01..D04), QA (E44-Q01..Q03) and security (E44-X01..X02) tickets.

**Story coverage (domains PAPER + ADMIN, E44 slice)**
| Story | Ticket |
|---|---|
| US-PAPER-002 Explicit Demo↔Live switching (live half) | E44-S02, E44-S03 |
| US-PAPER-003 Demo/Live isolation gating | E44-T02, E44-T03, E44-S03 |
| US-PAPER-007 Demo eligibility per manager | E44-S04 |
| US-ADMIN-007 Feature flags (safety-flag half) | E44-T04, E44-S01 |
| US-ADMIN-010 Security posture panel (gate + key-scope half) | E44-T05, E44-S01 |
| US-ADMIN-012 Live-trading enablement gate | E44-T04, E44-S01 |

## Out of scope
- The demo trading integration itself, paper P&L and reset, and the parity report (US-PAPER-001/004/005/006/008) — owned by **E38 Paper trading & demo/live parity** (R3).
- Kill-switch and risk caps mechanics — **E39** (R3); E44 only consumes them.
- The pen-test itself and its remediation — **E43**.
- Reconciliation, dead-man's-switch and the chaos suite — **E45**.
- The generic admin screens (users, roles, audit browser, health) — **E42**; E44 only adds the gate widgets onto SCR-137/SCR-145 and the eligibility control onto SCR-122.
- Android and any separate admin application (owner decision 2026-09-14).
- Non-Bybit exchanges and non-USDT-perp instruments.

## Acceptance criteria (epic outcome)
```gherkin
Scenario: Live is structurally unreachable until the gate passes
  Given a deployment where the Live-enablement gate has any of its four items outstanding
  When the owner opens SCR-145 and attempts to enable trading.live_enabled
  Then the toggle is disabled, the outstanding items are listed by name with a link to SCR-137
  And PUT /admin/feature-flags/trading.live_enabled returns 422 validation_failed / gate_evidence_required

Scenario: No process can cross the environment boundary
  Given a process booted with environment=live
  When it attempts any read or write against the demo Postgres schema or the demo QuestDB namespace
  Then the attempt fails at the connection/grant level, not merely in application code
  And the isolation assertion suite (E44-Q01) proves it in both directions

Scenario: A live-credentialed boot with an unsafe key refuses to start
  Given any configured key for a live account reports withdrawal scope enabled or an empty IP allowlist
  When the service starts with environment=live
  Then startup aborts with a fatal, actionable log line naming the account and the failing assertion
  And no listener is bound and no exchange session is opened

Scenario: Live is unmistakable everywhere
  Given the session environment is live
  Then SCR-010 chrome, every trading-capable panel badge (SCR-075) and every order confirmation restate LIVE as text plus icon plus pattern, never colour alone
  And confirm-on-every-order is ON by default and cannot be silenced with "don't ask again" in live
```

## Technical notes / design
- `Environment` is a single vocabulary shared by `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §1, the OpenAPI `Environment` schema and the Postgres `exchange_env` enum; the existing contract test `enum_parity_environment` must remain green.
- `Environment` (which credentials/account) and `ExecutionMode` (who filled it) stay orthogonal — never collapsed. Paper-ness is the `is_paper` boolean.
- Authorization stays the 4-tuple `(permission, account_id ∈ granted accounts, symbol ∈ allowed_symbols, environment enabled)` in a single `authorize()`; E44 adds no new permission for "live" (`docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §14).
- Flag resolution order and the environment-scoped override are already specified (`docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §16.2); E44 uses the `environment` override scope rather than inventing per-env flag tables.
- Error codes used by this epic: `live_trading_disabled`, `step_up_required`, `environment_mismatch`, `gate_evidence_required`, `live_not_permitted_for_user`.

## Test plan
Per-child; rolled up by E44-Q01..Q03. Epic-level gates: isolation assertion suite green in both directions; a Playwright E2E that walks gate-blocked → gate-satisfied → enable → switch → live badge → live order confirm; an axe-core pass over SCR-074/075/122/137/145; a security review sign-off from E44-X02.

## Security notes
This epic is the last structural barrier between the product and real money. Threats (STRIDE, modelled in E44-X01): spoofing a live session from a demo client; tampering with the flag value directly in Postgres; repudiation of who enabled live; information disclosure of live key scopes into logs; elevation of privilege by a manager without a live grant. Data classification: secrets (API keys, never logged), financial data (orders/positions). Every E44 ticket is `security`-labelled per `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §8.

## Accessibility notes
SCR-010/074/075/122/137/145 are all WCAG 2.2 AA surfaces. The demo/live distinction must survive greyscale and all three colour-vision simulations; the environment change is announced assertively; the switch is click-only and never hotkey-bindable.

## Performance notes
Environment switching completes in ≤2 s including private-subscription teardown/resubscribe and never leaves a half-switched state. Flag propagation to all sessions ≤2 s over the `system` topic. The environment leg of `authorize()` must not push the order-path check above the ≤5 ms p95 budget from US-ADMIN-003.

## Observability
Audit: `session.environment_switched` (high), `flag.changed` (high, with before/after + reason + evidence_url), `apikey.verify_failed`, `config.changed`, `system.startup`. Metrics: `cv_live_trading_enabled` gauge, `cv_environment_mismatch_rejections_total`, `cv_key_permission_assertion_failures_total`, `cv_environment_switch_seconds` histogram. Logs carry `environment` on every trading-path record; traces propagate it as a span attribute.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Every child ticket Done or explicitly descoped with a recorded disposition.
- [ ] R4 exit criteria 2 and 4 (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §8.3) demonstrably met.
- [ ] Coverage ≥90% on M1/M14/M17 touched modules (R4 gate), ≥80% frontend.
- [ ] `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`, `23-ws-protocol.md`, `24-internal-schemas.md`, `21-database-schema.md` updated to shipped behaviour; ADR-0016 merged.
- [ ] axe-core green + manual screen-reader pass on all touched screens.
- [ ] STRIDE model finalised, Critical/High closed, Security sign-off comment present.
- [ ] Epic-level QA regression + exploratory pass recorded; design QA signed off by the CDO delegate.
- [ ] Demoed to the Owner against staging; Owner acceptance recorded.
- [ ] Roadmap §3 points-convention footnote merged (E44-T06) and the engineering-only total re-checked against the register at epic close.

## Dependencies
`E38` (demo integration, environment switching skeleton), `E39` (kill-switch and risk caps that the gate reports on), `E43` (pen-test evidence is an input to the gate), `E42` (SCR-137/SCR-145/SCR-122 host screens), `E29` (OMS state whose storage is being split), `E27` (key vault and key metadata for the scope audit), `E09` (step-up authentication).

## Branch

## References

- docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md
- docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md, 04-security-program.md, 05-accessibility-standard.md, 06-performance-and-load-standard.md
- docs/plan/07-release-and-prr.md §6

- docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md CMP-074/075/095/139/175/178/179
- docs/plan/21-database-schema.md, 22-api-openapi.yaml, 23-ws-protocol.md, 24-internal-schemas.md
- docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md §3, §8

## Children dependency graph
```mermaid
graph TD
  D01[D01 wireframes] --> D02[D02 hi-fi gate+switch]
  D02 --> D03[D03 a11y+motion+handoff]
  D03 --> S01[S01 gate UI]
  D03 --> S02[S02 switch]
  D03 --> S03[S03 live visual language]
  D03 --> S04[S04 eligibility]
  K01[K01 storage split spike] --> T02[T02 storage separation]
  T01[T01 typed env + self-check] --> T02
  T01 --> T03[T03 cross-env guard]

```

## Agent guidance
How to pick the next ticket in this epic (multi-agent parallel execution):

**Dependency order** — do `K*` spikes and `D01` (research) first if present, then `T*`/`X*` foundational tech tasks in ascending number order, then `S*` stories (which consume the tech tasks), then `Q*` test-hardening tasks last so they exercise the finished surface.

**Parallel lanes** — tickets with disjoint `Repo paths to create/modify` (see each ticket's Agent execution brief) can run concurrently; tickets touching the same REST path, WS topic, DB table or `machines/*.json` file must NOT run concurrently — serialize by ticket number within that shared interface.

**Shared interfaces to agree first** — before starting any story in this epic, confirm the contract (OpenAPI/WS schema, DB migration, or statechart definition) touched by its blocking `T*`/`X*` ticket is already merged; do not design against a contract that is still in review.

title: Wireframe the live-enablement gate, hardened switch and live visual language
body:
## Context
The design-ahead rule (`docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md`, team & cadence) requires design Done ≥2 sprints before the consuming FE story. E44's frontend stories land in **S20-S21**, so wireframes run in **S18**.

E44 changes four existing surfaces rather than inventing new ones, so this is a *targeted* wireframe pass, not a new-product discovery: SCR-145 (Admin: feature flags) gains a blocked/unblocked gate treatment for `trading.live_enabled`; SCR-137 (Admin: security centre) gains the four-item gate checklist; SCR-074 (Environment switcher) gains the hardened live path; SCR-010/SCR-075 gain the pervasive live chrome; SCR-122 (Admin: user detail) gains the live-eligibility control.

The one genuinely new interaction is the **gate checklist**: a machine-checked/attested mixed list where some items are computed (key-permission audit results, kill-switch test record) and some are human attestations (pen-test sign-off, Owner authorisation), per US-ADMIN-012's NFR ("criteria are machine-checked where possible and explicitly attested where not, with the attester and date recorded"). A short research touch with the Owner is warranted for that item only.

Refs: `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-PAPER-002/003/007, US-ADMIN-010/012; `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-010, SCR-074, SCR-075, SCR-122, SCR-137, SCR-145; `docs/plan/07-release-and-prr.md` §6.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Research touch (1 session, 45 min, with the Owner)** on the gate checklist only: which of the four items they expect to be automatic, what evidence they want to see attached, and what "blocked" should say when several items are outstanding. Written as 3-5 numbered findings mapped to frames.
- **Lo-fi wireframes** in Figma page `CandleViewer / E44 Live gating`, covering every state declared in `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` for each screen:
  - SCR-145 gate row: `blocked by gate` (with the reason text and the link to SCR-137), `enabled`, `rollback available`, `requires reload`.
  - SCR-137 gate panel: `Live enablement blocked` with per-item status, `all four satisfied`, per-item evidence link, attester + date, last-scan timestamp.
  - SCR-074 live path: `switching` (closing subscriptions → re-authenticating → resubscribing, order entry blocked), `switched` (10 s full-width confirmation banner), `failed`, `not permitted`, plus a new state **`blocked: gate closed`**.
  - SCR-010 + SCR-075 live chrome: chrome band, per-panel badge placement for ticket, group ticket, ladder, positions grid, algo monitor and chart trading overlay, and floating windows.
  - SCR-122 live-eligibility control: demo-only, live-granted, revoked-with-open-positions (reduce-only) per US-PAPER-007.
- **IA note**: the gate lives on SCR-137 as the source of truth and is *mirrored read-only* on SCR-145; the enable action itself is on SCR-145. Documented so the two do not drift.
- A component-reuse audit against `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md`: CMP-004 Toggle, CMP-028 Callout/Banner, CMP-036 KeyValueRow, CMP-043 Dialog, CMP-044 ConfirmDialog (`variant="typed"`), CMP-050 Card, CMP-074 EnvBanner, CMP-075 EnvBadgeLocal, CMP-087 AdminLayout, CMP-093 AuditActionTrigger, CMP-095 FeatureFlagChip, CMP-139 EnvironmentAwareOrderGuard, CMP-175 KeyPermissionBadge, CMP-178 SystemHealthTile, CMP-179 FeatureFlagRow. Any gap is raised as a design-system request, never an ad-hoc one-off.

## Out of scope
- Hi-fi visuals, tokens, motion (E44-D02/D03).
- Redesign of the admin shell, users table, audit browser or health tiles (E42).
- The demo-side switch path and parity report (E38).
- Any new screen ID — E44 introduces none.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every declared state exists as a frame
  When the CDO delegate reviews the wireframe set
  Then every state listed for SCR-074, SCR-075, SCR-137, SCR-145 and SCR-122 in docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md exists as a frame
  And the new "blocked: gate closed" state on SCR-074 is drawn with its explanatory copy

Scenario: The gate is legible when several items are outstanding
  Given three of the four gate items are outstanding
  Then the SCR-145 frame names all three in text with the link to SCR-137
  And no frame relies on colour alone to express blocked-ness

Scenario: No invented components
  When the component-reuse audit is reviewed
  Then every element maps to an existing CMP-nnn entry, or carries an explicit design-system request ticket reference
```

## Technical notes / design
Copy must avoid advice framing (risk R9) and must state consequences plainly. The gate's four items are fixed by `docs/plan/07-release-and-prr.md` §6 and may not be renamed by design: Pen-test, Key-permission audit, Kill-switch test, Owner sign-off.

## Test plan
N/A (design artefact). Verification is the sign-off review below.

## Security notes
Wireframes must never depict a real API key, a real Bybit UID, or an evidence URL pointing at a private artefact. Placeholder data only.

## Accessibility notes
Every frame annotates the text equivalent of each status; the switch control is annotated "click-only, never hotkey-bindable" per US-PAPER-002.

## Performance notes
N/A.

## Observability
N/A.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Research findings memo published with 3-5 numbered findings, each traced to a frame.
- [ ] All declared states drawn; component-reuse audit attached.
- [ ] IA note on SCR-137 vs SCR-145 ownership recorded.
- [ ] CDO delegate review passed; ticket Status Done ≥2 sprints before E44-S01..S04.

## Dependencies
Needs E42's admin-shell wireframes (SCR-137/145/122 base layouts) and E38's existing SCR-074 demo-side frames as the baseline to extend.

## Branch
`design/e44-live-gating-wireframes` (Figma-first; repo branch only for the findings memo).

## References
- docs/plan/07-release-and-prr.md §6
- docs/plan/11-user-stories.md US-PAPER-002/003/007, US-ADMIN-010/012
- docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md SCR-010/074/075/122/137/145
- docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md

## Agent execution brief
**Read first**
1. AGENTS.md §0 (read-order) and §3 (how to pick up a ticket)
2. `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md`

**Repo paths to create/modify**
- `apps/web/src/features/ticket/` (feature code), `packages/ui/src/trading/` (shared components, if reused ≥2 features)

**Interfaces you must not break**
- None beyond what is already named in this ticket's Technical notes / References.

**Commands**
- `pnpm --filter @candleviewer/web lint`
- `pnpm --filter @candleviewer/web typecheck`
- `pnpm --filter @candleviewer/web test`
- `pnpm test:a11y`

**Branch & PR**
- Branch: `design/e44-live-gating-wireframes`
- PR title: `E44-D01: Wireframe the live-enablement gate, hardened switch and live visual language`
- Body includes: `Closes #<issue-number-for-E44-D01>`
- Required reviewers (CODEOWNERS): @CandleViewer/backend @CandleViewer/architecture
- Labels: carry over this ticket's labels (design, ux-research, type/design, area/oms-execution, priority/p0, a11y)

**Done means**
- Research findings memo published with 3-5 numbered findings, each traced to a frame.
- All declared states drawn; component-reuse audit attached.
- IA note on SCR-137 vs SCR-145 ownership recorded.
- CDO delegate review passed; ticket Status Done ≥2 sprints before E44-S01..S04.

**Do NOT**
- Do not exceed the ~400 LOC PR diff guideline (AGENTS.md §3); split into follow-up tickets if the change grows.
- Do not implement anything listed under this ticket's own 'Out of scope' section.

**If blocked**
- Comment on the GitHub issue for `E44-D01` naming the exact blocking key (e.g. one of: Needs E42's admin-shell wireframes (SCR-137/145/122 base layouts) and E38's existing SCR-074 demo-side frames as the baseline to extend.); move ticket Status → Blocked; never silently work around a failing gate or a missing dependency ticket.

## Agent-delivery adaptations (owner decision 2026-09-25)
Delivery is executed by parallel AI agents with a single human owner (`@basiltt`). Where this ticket's text assumes the original 15-person org, apply these substitutions — they are binding and satisfy the corresponding DoR/DoD items:
- **Architect / CDO / Security-engineer sign-off or countersignature** → the **owner's** `approved` comment on this issue, or owner merge of the PR. No other human role exists. Do not block on a missing countersignature — proceed and record "owner approval pending" in the PR.
- **Design tooling**: *Figma* → **Penpot** (`docs/design/README.md`); frames on a page named after this ticket; exports via `docs/design/_tools/penpot_export.py`. Bind only to semantic tokens in `packages/ui/tokens/`.
- **Moderated usability / participant sessions** → a documented **heuristic evaluation** (Nielsen + the trading-specific heuristics in `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`), a written session protocol ready for the owner to run later, and an **owner walkthrough** checklist posted on the issue. Never fabricate participants, timings or quotes; label all findings `(heuristic)`.
- **CVD / contrast validation** → computed programmatically (WCAG contrast matrix over the token JSON; CVD simulation via a documented script), attached as artefacts.
- **Spikes**: findings go to `docs/plan/spikes/<KEY>.md` via a normal PR (branch `spike/<epic>-<slug>`); any ADR named by the spike uses the **next free number** in `docs/plan/27-adrs/` (ADR-0001…0016 are taken).
- **Dependencies**: `blocked_by` now lists the concrete prerequisite tickets (not whole epics). Start when those are **merged** (In Test or Done).
- Anything that genuinely needs a human that is not the owner (external pen-test vendor, legal) stays as-is and is flagged `needs-owner` on the issue.

title: Hi-fi designs for SCR-137/SCR-145 gate and SCR-074 hardened switch
body:
## Context
Turns the E44-D01 wireframes for the two admin gate surfaces and the environment switcher into token-accurate hi-fi designs that engineering can build from without asking questions. These are the screens where a mistake enables real-money trading, so the visual language must make "blocked" and "enabled" unmistakable and must make the enable action feel as heavy as it is.

Refs: `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-074, SCR-137, SCR-145; `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md` (tokens, density, theming).

## Scope / Deliverables
- Hi-fi frames (light + dark, comfortable + compact density) for:
  - **SCR-145** feature-flag row for `trading.live_enabled`: disabled toggle with the blocking reason inline, the link to SCR-137, the step-up requirement indicator, and the enabled/rollback-available variants. Uses CMP-179 FeatureFlagRow, CMP-095 FeatureFlagChip, CMP-004 Toggle, CMP-093 AuditActionTrigger.
  - **SCR-137** gate panel: four rows (Pen-test, Key-permission audit, Kill-switch test, Owner sign-off), each with machine-checked vs attested provenance, evidence link, attester + date, last-evaluated timestamp, and the all-clear state. Uses CMP-050 Card, CMP-036 KeyValueRow, CMP-028 Callout, CMP-175 KeyPermissionBadge, CMP-178 SystemHealthTile.
  - **SCR-074** hardened switch: the LIVE path with typed confirmation + 2FA, the working-demo-orders statement, the transition progress, the 10 s post-switch banner, the gate-closed refusal, and the "owner hasn't enabled Live for your account" refusal. Uses CMP-043 Dialog, CMP-044 ConfirmDialog `variant="typed"`, CMP-074 EnvBanner, CMP-027 InlineError.
- Redlines: spacing, type scale, token names (`color.env.demo`, `color.env.live`, `color.status.success/danger`), focus rings, minimum hit targets.
- Greyscale and colour-vision-simulation exports proving the demo/live distinction survives without colour.
- Copy deck for every string, reviewed against risk R9 (no advice framing) and stating consequences in plain language.

title: Spike: choose the physical environment-separation mechanism for OMS state
body:
## Context
R4 exit criterion 4 (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §8.3) demands a *test* proving that "no demo credential, cache entry, OMS row or storage partition can be read or written by a live-configured process and vice versa". Application-level `WHERE env = ...` filtering cannot satisfy that: a missing predicate in one query silently breaks it. We need a mechanism where the database itself refuses.

Three candidate mechanisms exist and the choice has real trade-offs against our single-node WSL/VPS deployment (`docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md`), our migration tooling, and the existing schema in `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` (where `exchange_accounts.env` already exists and trigger `trg_ea_env_parent` already forbids cross-env parenting).

## Scope / Deliverables
Timebox: **3 days**. Answer, with measured evidence:
1. **Mechanism for Postgres.** Compare: (a) one Postgres *schema* per environment (`oms_live`, `oms_demo`) with a per-environment role granted only on its own schema and `search_path` fixed at connection time; (b) separate databases; (c) row-level security policies on shared tables. Evaluate against: strength of the refusal (does a missing predicate still leak?), migration complexity with our Alembic-style tooling, connection-pool cost, backup/restore ergonomics (`SCR-146` restore drill), and how reference data (instruments, users, audit) that is legitimately shared is handled.
2. **Mechanism for QuestDB.** Namespace/table-prefix per environment vs separate instance; measure ingestion overhead. Note that market data is mainnet even for demo trading (`docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §, `market_data.env` default `live`), so the split applies to OMS-derived series only.
3. **Which tables move.** Produce the definitive list: which tables are environment-partitioned (orders, executions, positions, trade groups, algo state, paper state) and which are global (users, roles, audit, instruments, recorded symbols, workspaces). Justify each.
4. **Cache and in-process state.** How the in-memory OMS state, flag cache and key cache are keyed so a single process can never hold both environments' mutable state.
5. **Prototype** the chosen mechanism far enough to run the negative test: a live-role connection attempting `SELECT` on the demo schema must fail with a permission error.

Decision criteria agreed up front: **the refusal must come from the database's grant model, not from application code**; migration must remain a single ordered sequence; added p95 order-path latency must be <2 ms.

## Out of scope
- Implementing the migration (E44-T02).
- Backup/restore automation (E45 / E42 SCR-146).
- Multi-tenant or multi-exchange generalisation.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A recommendation with evidence
  When the spike closes
  Then a comparison table covers all three Postgres options and both QuestDB options against every stated criterion
  And a single recommendation is made with the measured p95 order-path latency delta

Scenario: The negative test is demonstrated
  Given the prototype of the recommended mechanism
  When a live-role connection queries a demo-schema table
  Then it fails with a database permission error, evidenced by a captured session transcript

Scenario: Decision recorded
  Then ADR-0016 is drafted from the findings, and follow-up tickets exist for the chosen path
```

## Technical notes / design
Candidate (a) sketch: roles `cv_live` and `cv_demo`; `GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA oms_live TO cv_live` only; `ALTER ROLE cv_live SET search_path = oms_live, shared`; shared reference tables live in schema `shared` with `SELECT` to both and `INSERT/UPDATE` restricted by existing RBAC. Migrations run as a superuser-ish migration role and are applied to every environment schema from one versioned source, so the schemas can never drift.

## Test plan
Prototype-level only: a pytest that opens a `cv_live` connection and asserts `psycopg.errors.InsufficientPrivilege` on demo-schema access; a pgbench-style measurement of connection + query overhead.

## Security notes
This spike decides the strength of the single most important isolation boundary in the product. Record explicitly what the mechanism does **not** protect against (e.g. a process configured with the wrong credentials entirely — covered by E44-T01's startup self-check).

## Accessibility notes
N/A.

## Performance notes
Report added p95 on the order path and added connection-establishment cost; budget <2 ms p95 added, consistent with the ≤5 ms risk-check overhead in US-ADMIN-003.

## Observability
Recommend the metric/label shape for environment (a `environment` label on OMS metrics vs separate metric names) as part of the finding.

title: Make environment a typed first-class setting with a fail-fast startup self-check
body:
## Context
Today environment is a value carried on rows and requests. E44 makes it a **resolved, validated, process-wide fact**: one `ExchangeConfig.environment` (`docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §16.1) decides hosts, credential set, storage namespace and which accounts are even visible. Anything that disagrees with it must fail at boot rather than at 3am on the order path.

The cross-field validators already specified in `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §16.1 — `exchange.environment == "live"` requires the `live_trading` flag **and** a recorded pen-test completion date; `bind_host` must not be `0.0.0.0` in prod — are implemented here, together with the **key-permission startup assertion** demanded by `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §8.2 ("a startup self-check that refuses to boot with live credentials if any configured key fails the withdrawal-OFF / IP-whitelist assertion").

## Scope / Deliverables
- `EnvironmentContext` value object in the M1 config module: `environment`, `environment_allowlist` (default `("demo",)`; `live` added only when the gate is satisfied; `testnet` never user-selectable per `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §8 testnet note), resolved once at startup and injected — never re-read from a mutable global.
- Config validators (fail-fast, abort boot with a non-zero exit and an actionable message):
  - `environment == "live"` ⇒ `live_trading` flag ON **and** a recorded pen-test completion date present.
  - `environment == "live"` ⇒ every configured `exchange_accounts` row selected by this process has `env='live'`; a demo row in a live-configured process is fatal.
  - `bind_host != 0.0.0.0` when `env == "prod"`.
  - `oms.block_on_postgres_unavailable` cannot be `False` in prod.
- **Startup key self-check**: for every configured key, call the Bybit key-info endpoint through the existing adapter (E27 key vault) and assert (i) withdrawal scope absent, (ii) IP allowlist non-empty and containing the deployment egress IP, (iii) scopes limited to read+trade. Failure in `live` ⇒ boot abort. Failure in `demo` ⇒ loud startup warning plus a `security` finding surfaced on SCR-137, not an abort.
- Propagation: `environment` added as a structured-log field, a trace span attribute and a label on OMS metrics, on every request-scoped context.
- `GET /auth/session` and the WS `auth_ok` frame already carry `allowed_environments` (`docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md`); wire them to `environment_allowlist` ∩ the user's grant so the client can never offer an environment the server would refuse.
- Config keys introduced/confirmed: `CV__EXCHANGE__ENVIRONMENT`, `CV__EXCHANGE__ENVIRONMENT_ALLOWLIST`, `CV__SECURITY__PENTEST_COMPLETED_AT`, `CV__SECURITY__EGRESS_IP`.

## Out of scope
- Physical storage separation (E44-T02) and the route guard (E44-T03).
- The flag's enable endpoint and gate evaluation (E44-T04).
- The standalone key-scope audit report tool (E44-T05) — this ticket does the *boot assertion*; T05 does the *audit record*.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Live boot with the gate closed is refused
  Given CV__EXCHANGE__ENVIRONMENT=live and the live_trading flag is OFF
  When the service starts
  Then it exits non-zero before binding a listener
  And the log states "environment=live requires live_trading flag ON and a recorded pen-test completion date"

Scenario: Live boot with an unsafe key is refused
  Given a configured live key whose Bybit-reported scopes include withdrawal
  When the service starts
  Then it exits non-zero, names the account label and the failing assertion, and never opens an exchange session
  And the key secret does not appear anywhere in the output

Scenario: Demo boot with an unsafe key warns but starts
  Given the same condition with CV__EXCHANGE__ENVIRONMENT=demo
  Then the service starts, emits a WARNING log and records a security finding visible on SCR-137

Scenario: The client cannot be offered an unavailable environment
  Given environment_allowlist is ("demo",)
  When a client authenticates over REST and over the WS
  Then GET /auth/session and the auth_ok frame both report allowed_environments = ["demo"]
```

## Technical notes / design
Pydantic model validators on `AppConfig`; the key self-check runs after config validation and before the HTTP listener binds, in a dedicated `startup_selfcheck()` coroutine with a 10 s per-key timeout and no retries (a flaky exchange in `live` is still a refusal — operator re-runs). Assertion results are cached in memory and exposed to `GET /admin/security/summary` via the shape defined in E44-T05. Error codes: `config_invalid`, `key_permission_assertion_failed`, `environment_account_mismatch`.

## Test plan
- Unit: each validator, both directions, including the `testnet`-not-selectable rule; `str(config)` contains no secret (existing assertion extended).
- Contract: `enum_parity_environment` stays green; `allowed_environments` matches between REST and WS for the same token.
- Integration: boot the app against recorded Bybit key-info fixtures — safe key (boots), withdrawal-enabled key (aborts in live, warns in demo), empty-allowlist key (aborts in live), exchange timeout (aborts in live).
- Coverage target ≥90% on M1 touched code (R4 module policy).

## Security notes
Threats (E44-X01): a misconfigured deployment silently trading live; key material leaking into logs or crash dumps. Controls: fail-fast validation, `SecretStr`, redacted effective-config dump, no retry of key checks. Data classification: secrets. Security review label required.

## Accessibility notes
N/A (backend).

## Performance notes
Startup self-check adds ≤10 s worst case (one round trip per key, bounded); not on any request path. The `environment` log/label addition must not measurably change order-path latency (≤0.2 ms).

## Observability
Logs: `system.startup` audit event including environment and the self-check outcome per account (no secrets). Metrics: `cv_key_permission_assertion_failures_total{account}`, `cv_startup_selfcheck_duration_seconds`, `cv_live_trading_enabled` gauge.

title: Separate OMS state storage per environment (Postgres schemas, QuestDB namespaces)
body:
## Context
Implements the mechanism chosen by E44-K01 so that R4 exit criterion 4 is provable: no live-configured process can read or write demo state, and vice versa, enforced by the database's grant model rather than by application predicates.

`docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` already gives us the vocabulary (`exchange_env` enum, `exchange_accounts.env`, trigger `trg_ea_env_parent`, `trade_groups.tg_paper_env`) and the principle that demo is a *separate account row*, never a flag on the live row. This ticket extends that principle from rows to storage.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Postgres migration** creating the environment-partitioned schemas and the `shared` schema, per the E44-K01 recommendation; moving the OMS-owned mutable tables (orders, order events, executions, positions, trade groups and membership snapshots, algo state, paper state) into the per-environment schemas; leaving global tables (users, roles, bindings, audit, instruments, recorded symbols, workspaces, rules, alerts, journal) in `shared`.
- **Roles and grants**: `cv_live` and `cv_demo` roles with `USAGE`/DML only on their own schema plus the agreed access to `shared`; `search_path` pinned per role; the application connects as exactly one of them, chosen by `EnvironmentContext` from E44-T01.
- **Migration tooling change**: one ordered migration sequence applied to every environment schema from a single source, with a CI check that the schemas are structurally identical (no drift).
- **QuestDB namespacing** for OMS-derived series per the K01 recommendation; market-data tables stay single-namespace because market data is mainnet for both environments (`docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §`market_data.env` default `live`).
- **In-process state keying**: OMS in-memory state, key cache and flag cache keyed so a process holds exactly one environment's mutable state; a startup assertion that the cache key matches `EnvironmentContext`.
- **Data migration** of existing demo-era rows from R3 into the `demo` schema, with a reversible down-migration and a row-count reconciliation report.
- **Negative-access test module** (the artefact R4 exit criterion 4 names) asserting refusal in both directions at the connection level.

## Out of scope
- The route-level guard (E44-T03) — that is defence in depth *above* this layer.
- Backup/restore per environment (E42 SCR-146 / E45 restore drill).
- Splitting the audit log (deliberately global and append-only: a cross-environment action must be visible in one chain, `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-ADMIN-008).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Cross-environment access is refused by the database
  Given the application is connected as cv_live
  When it issues any SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE against a demo-schema OMS table
  Then Postgres raises an insufficient-privilege error
  And the same holds symmetrically for cv_demo against the live schema

Scenario: Schemas never drift
  Given the migration sequence has been applied
  When the CI structural-comparison check runs
  Then the live and demo schemas are structurally identical, and any difference fails the build

Scenario: Existing demo data survives the split
  Given R3 demo orders, executions, positions and trade groups exist
  When the migration runs
  Then every row is present in the demo schema with identical values, proven by the row-count and checksum reconciliation report
  And the down-migration restores the pre-split arrangement

Scenario: A process cannot hold both environments' state
  Given a process booted as demo
  When it attempts to populate an OMS cache entry keyed live
  Then the attempt raises and is logged as a programming error, caught in CI by the assertion test
```

## Technical notes / design
Follow K01's recommendation verbatim; deviations require an ADR amendment. Connection pooling: one pool per process bound to one role — no role switching (`SET ROLE`) at runtime, since that reintroduces an application-level decision. Migrations run under a dedicated migration role that has rights on all schemas; the application role never does. The structural-comparison check diffs `information_schema` output between the two schemas.

## Test plan
- Unit: cache-key assertion; migration helpers.
- Integration: apply migrations from empty and from an R3-shaped fixture database; run the reconciliation report; run the negative-access suite in both directions; run the down-migration and re-apply.
- Perf: measure order-path p95 before/after the split; budget <2 ms added (K01 criterion) against `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md`.
- Chaos-adjacent: verify behaviour when the environment's schema is missing at boot (must abort, not create silently).
- Coverage ≥90% on M14-touched code.

## Security notes
This is the structural isolation boundary. Threats: privilege creep if the app role is granted more than its schema; a migration accidentally granting cross-schema rights. Controls: a CI grant-assertion test that enumerates the actual grants of `cv_live`/`cv_demo` and fails on any unexpected privilege. Data classification: financial data. Security review required.

## Accessibility notes
N/A.

## Performance notes
Report added p95 on the order path and added connection-establishment cost; fail the ticket if >2 ms p95 added. QuestDB ingestion overhead from namespacing must be within the ingestion budget in `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md`.

## Observability
Metrics gain an `environment` label. Add `cv_db_grant_assertion_failures_total`. Log the resolved schema and role at startup. Audit `config.changed` if the environment binding changes.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Migration, roles/grants, QuestDB namespacing and cache keying implemented.
- [ ] Negative-access suite and grant-assertion test in CI and green.
- [ ] Reconciliation report attached; down-migration exercised.
- [ ] Perf measurement attached and within budget.
- [ ] `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` updated with the schema layout and grant model.
- [ ] Security engineer review comment present.

title: Enforce the cross-environment guard in one middleware on every trading route
body:
## Context
US-PAPER-003's NFR is explicit: isolation is "enforced in one middleware layer with tests covering every trading route". Its third scenario is the one that matters — "Given a crafted request targets a live account from a demo session, Then it is rejected with 403 and audited as a high-severity event".

This is defence in depth above the storage split (E44-T02): even if a query were mis-scoped, the request never reaches it.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Extend the single `authorize()` function (`docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §14) so the environment leg of the 4-tuple `(permission, account ∈ grants, symbol ∈ allowed_symbols, environment enabled)` is evaluated for **every** trading-capable route — no endpoint hand-rolls it. No new permission is introduced for "live" (explicitly rejected in §14 and `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §: the live/demo distinction is the environment leg plus the `live_trading` flag).
- The guard compares three facts and requires all to agree: the process `EnvironmentContext`, the session environment, and the target account's `exchange_accounts.env`. Any disagreement ⇒ `403` with error code `environment_mismatch` and an RFC 9457 body naming which fact disagreed (without leaking the other environment's account identifiers).
- **Trade-group invariant**: a group may not contain accounts from two environments — enforced at creation, at membership change and again at submit, matching the existing `tg_paper_env` check constraint (`docs/plan/21-database-schema.md`).
- **Live-flag leg**: when the target environment is `live`, the guard additionally requires `live_trading` ON (error `live_trading_disabled`) and, for the capabilities marked `(step-up)` in `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §7.2.2, an elevated session (`step_up_required`).
- **Route inventory test**: an automated test enumerates every route tagged as trading-capable in `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` (orders, order amend/cancel, positions actions, trade-group submit/amend/cancel, algo control, rule arming) and asserts each is covered by the guard; adding a trading route without guard coverage fails CI.
- WS parity: subscriptions and any environment-bearing frame respect `allowed_environments` from `auth_ok`; a `sub` for a private topic outside the session environment is rejected.
- Audit: `403` from this guard emits a high-severity audit event with actor, session environment, target account, route and correlation id.

## Out of scope
- Risk caps, kill-switch and lockouts (E39) — orthogonal legs evaluated elsewhere in the same `authorize()`.
- Client-side guarding (CMP-139 wrapper, E44-S03).
- The flag's own write path (E44-T04).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A crafted cross-environment request is refused and audited
  Given a session whose environment is demo
  When it POSTs an order targeting an exchange account with env='live'
  Then the response is 403 with error code environment_mismatch
  And a high-severity audit event records actor, route, session environment and target account
  And no order row is created in either schema

Scenario: Every trading route is covered
  When the route-inventory test runs over docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml
  Then every trading-capable operation is asserted to pass through the guard
  And adding a new trading operation without coverage fails the build

Scenario: A mixed trade group cannot be created or submitted
  Given a trade group containing a demo account
  When a live account is added, or the group is submitted from a live session
  Then the request is refused at creation time and again at submit time, with the reason naming the offending account

Scenario: Live with the flag off is refused
  Given live_trading is OFF
  When a live-targeted order is submitted from an otherwise valid live session
  Then the response is 403 live_trading_disabled and the attempt is audited
```

## Technical notes / design
Implemented as a dependency/middleware that resolves the target account(s) from the request model before the handler runs, so the check cannot be skipped by a handler forgetting to call it. Ordering inside `authorize()`: permission → account scope → symbol allowlist → environment → flag → step-up, failing on the first, with the error code of the first failure (avoids leaking which later legs would also have failed). Performance: the check is pure and reads from the in-memory account/flag caches; no database round trip on the order path.

## Test plan
- Unit: the guard's truth table across process env × session env × account env × flag state × elevation (exhaustive, generated).
- Contract: every `403` shape conforms to the RFC 9457 error schema in `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`.
- Integration: the four AC scenarios end to end against a two-schema fixture database.
- E2E: Playwright attempt of a cross-environment action via a tampered client store, asserting the server refuses (extended in E44-Q01).
- Perf: assert the environment+flag legs add ≤1 ms p95 to the order path (within the ≤5 ms total risk-check budget).
- Coverage ≥90%.

## Security notes
Threats (E44-X01): elevation of privilege (demo user reaching live), spoofing (client asserting an environment it was not granted), repudiation (a refused attempt not recorded). Controls: server-side-only decision, high-severity audit on refusal, no client-supplied environment ever trusted. The error body must not enumerate accounts from the other environment. Data classification: financial data. Security review required.

## Accessibility notes
N/A (backend); the client rendering of these refusals is specified in E44-S02/S03.

## Performance notes
≤1 ms p95 added; verified by the OMS benchmark in `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md`.

## Observability
Metric `cv_environment_mismatch_rejections_total{route,reason}`; audit action reuses the existing vocabulary (`order.rejected` plus a dedicated high-severity security event); traces record the guard decision as a span attribute.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Guard implemented in one place; route-inventory test in CI.
- [ ] All AC scenarios covered by automated tests.
- [ ] `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` documents `environment_mismatch` and `live_trading_disabled` on every trading route.
- [ ] Perf assertion green; coverage ≥90%.
- [ ] Security engineer review comment present.

title: Implement the live_trading gate: evidence-bound flag write and gate evaluation API
body:
## Context
> **Re-scoped 2026-09-24 for full xstate-statemachine adoption (ADR-0016 Accepted):** the three-state live-trading gate (locked→eligible→enabled) is built directly on the library via the factory; the evidence-binding and audit logic that feeds the gate's guards stays as is.

`trading.live_enabled` (internal registry key `live_trading`, `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §16.2, kill-switch flag, default `false`) is the single mechanism that can enable live trading — the roadmap states it outright: "No live code path exists before R4. The environment gate (E44) is the only mechanism that can enable live, and it defaults OFF" (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §12).

`docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` already special-cases `PUT /admin/feature-flags/{flagKey}` for this key: enabling requires `reason` and `evidence_url`, otherwise `validation_failed` / `gate_evidence_required`. This ticket implements that, plus the **gate evaluation** that decides whether the toggle is even offered, mirroring the four items of `docs/plan/07-release-and-prr.md` §6.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Implement the `B17` lifecycle as `statechart/machines/B17.live_gate.machine.json` (committed by E50-S02, hash-locked). Do not hand-write the state enum or transition table.
- Build it only through `statechart.factory.build('live_gate', lane=…)`, and restore it only through `statechart.persistence.restore`.

  1. `pentest` — attested: requires a recorded completion date + evidence URL (the same fact E44-T01's config validator reads).
  2. `key_permission_audit` — machine: satisfied when E44-T05's latest audit run covers every configured account and every assertion passed, and the run is not older than 30 days.
  3. `kill_switch_test` — attested with machine assist: requires a recorded successful kill-switch exercise (E39's audit trail supplies the evidence of engage/release).
  4. `owner_signoff` — attested: Owner identity, date, and a free-text authorisation reference.
- **Read API**: gate state folded into `GET /admin/security/summary` (`SecuritySummary` gains a `live_enablement_gate` member) and returned alongside the flag on `GET /admin/feature-flags` so SCR-145 can render the blocking reason without a second call.
- **Write API**: `PUT /admin/feature-flags/trading.live_enabled` enforcing, in order: `flags:write` permission → elevated session (step-up) → gate fully satisfied → `reason` non-empty → `evidence_url` well-formed. Failures return `403 step_up_required`, `422 gate_evidence_required`, or `422 validation_failed` with the outstanding item keys.
- **Attestation endpoints**: recording an attested item is itself an audited, step-up-gated, owner-only action; attestations are append-only (a correction is a new attestation superseding the old, never an edit).
- **Propagation**: a flag change broadcasts on the `system` WS topic (`SystemUpdate`, `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §15.9) within 2 s; turning the flag OFF takes effect immediately on the order path (it is a kill-switch-class flag) and existing positions remain manageable in reduce-only mode (US-ADMIN-012 emergency re-disable).
- **Audit**: `flag.changed` high severity with before/after, reason, evidence URL and actor; a dedicated high-severity event for the enablement itself.

- The UI (E44-S01).
- The key-scope audit run itself (E44-T05) — consumed here as an input.
- The kill-switch mechanism (E39) — consumed here as evidence.
- Generic feature-flag CRUD and the flag cache (E42 / existing flag module).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Enabling with an outstanding gate item is refused
  Given the key_permission_audit item is outstanding
  When PUT /admin/feature-flags/trading.live_enabled is called with value true, a reason and an evidence_url
  Then the response is 422 with code gate_evidence_required and the body lists key_permission_audit

Scenario: Enabling without step-up is refused
  Given all four gate items are satisfied and the session is not elevated
  When the enable call is made

Scenario: A satisfied gate enables live and propagates
  Given all four gate items are satisfied and the session is elevated
  When the owner enables the flag with a reason and an evidence URL

Scenario: Emergency re-disable stops new live orders but not management
  Given live trading is enabled and a live position is open
  When the owner disables the flag
  Then new live orders are refused with live_trading_disabled within 2 seconds
  And reduce-only actions on the open position still succeed

Scenario: A stale key audit reopens the gate
  Given the last key-permission audit run is 31 days old

```

title: Build the production key-permission audit tool reporting Bybit-declared scopes
body:
## Context
R4 exit criterion 2 is unusually specific: "The audit record includes the Bybit-reported scopes, not just the app's belief about them" (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §8.3). The roadmap's E44 scope line calls for "production key-permission audit tooling that prints the actual Bybit-reported key scopes for the audit record".

This is distinct from E44-T01's boot assertion: T01 *refuses to start*; T05 *produces the durable evidence record* that the Live-enablement gate (E44-T04) consumes and that the Owner reviews.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A CLI entry point `python -m candleviewer.security.key_audit` and an equivalent owner-only, step-up-gated API action, both producing the same immutable `KeyPermissionAuditRun` record: run id, started/finished timestamps, actor, app version, and per account: account label, Bybit UID, environment, **the raw scope list exactly as Bybit reports it**, withdrawal flag, IP allowlist entries, key creation and expiry dates, and a pass/fail per assertion (withdrawal OFF, IP allowlist non-empty and containing the deployment egress IP, scopes ⊆ {read, trade}).
- Human-readable output (a table for the audit record) and a machine-readable JSON artefact; both redact key IDs to a stable prefix and never emit secret material.
- Persisted as append-only rows feeding `GET /admin/security/summary` and rendered on SCR-128 (key health) and SCR-137 (security centre) via CMP-175 KeyPermissionBadge.
- Divergence detection: when Bybit's reported scopes differ from the app's stored belief about a key, the run fails that account, emits `apikey.verify_failed` and raises a security finding with the exact difference.
- A scheduled run (daily) plus on-demand; the gate item in E44-T04 requires a passing run newer than 30 days.

## Out of scope
- Rotating or revoking keys (E27).
- Changing Bybit-side settings — the tool only reads and reports; remediation is a manual Bybit action with a link and instructions.
- Boot-time refusal (E44-T01).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The record contains exchange-reported scopes
  When an audit run completes against a configured account
  Then the record contains the scope list exactly as returned by Bybit, alongside the app's stored belief
  And no secret material appears in either the human-readable or JSON output

Scenario: A withdrawal-enabled key fails the run
  Given a key whose Bybit-reported permissions include withdrawal
  Then the run marks that account failed, emits apikey.verify_failed, and the key_permission_audit gate item becomes outstanding

Scenario: Divergence between belief and reality is reported
  Given the app believes a key is read+trade but Bybit reports read+trade+transfer
  Then the run fails the account and the report names the exact extra scope

Scenario: The run is immutable
  Given a completed audit run
  When any attempt is made to update or delete it
  Then it is refused by the database grant model, consistent with the append-only audit policy
```

## Technical notes / design
Uses the E27 key vault to obtain credentials in memory only and the Bybit v5 key-information endpoint through the existing adapter. Rate limiting: one call per key with the standard governor; a `10018` response retries with backoff and, on exhaustion, marks the account `indeterminate` (not `pass`) — indeterminate keeps the gate item outstanding. Errors: `key_audit_unreachable`, `key_audit_divergence`, `key_audit_assertion_failed`.

## Test plan
- Unit: assertion evaluation per scope combination; redaction; indeterminate handling.
- Integration: recorded Bybit fixtures for safe key, withdrawal-enabled key, empty-allowlist key, divergent-scope key, rate-limited response, timeout.
- Contract: the `SecuritySummary` extension matches `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`.
- Security: a test asserting no secret appears in stdout, the JSON artefact, or the log.
- Coverage ≥90%.

## Security notes
Threats (E44-X01): information disclosure of key material into an audit artefact that is then shared; a forged "pass" record enabling the gate. Controls: redaction plus an explicit no-secret test; append-only storage; the run record signed/hash-chained with the audit chain so a forged record breaks verification. Data classification: secrets + security metadata. Security review required and the Security engineer is the reviewer of record.

## Accessibility notes
The rendered result on SCR-128/SCR-137 uses CMP-175, which must state "Withdrawal: OFF ✓" affirmatively — absence of a chip is not an acceptable representation (`docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-175).

## Performance notes
One exchange round trip per key, run off the request path; a full run over all accounts completes in ≤30 s.

## Observability
Metrics: `cv_key_audit_runs_total{result}`, `cv_key_audit_account_status{account,status}`, `cv_key_audit_age_seconds`. Audit: `apikey.verify_failed` on failure; the run itself recorded. Alert when the newest passing run exceeds 30 days.

- [ ] Coverage ≥90%; no-secret test green; Security engineer sign-off.

```gherkin

  Given the pen-test attestation and the key-permission audit are outstanding
  When the owner opens SCR-145
  Then the trading.live_enabled toggle is disabled
  And the row names both outstanding items in text with a link to SCR-137
  And SCR-137 shows both rows as outstanding with their provenance and last-evaluated timestamp

Scenario: Gate open, enablement succeeds and is audited
  Given all four gate items are satisfied
  When the owner enables live with step-up, a typed confirmation, a reason and an evidence URL

  And the audit entry for flag.changed records before/after, reason, evidence URL and actor

Scenario: Enablement attempted without evidence
  When the owner submits the enable form with an empty evidence URL
  Then the form blocks submission with a field-level error, and no request is sent

Scenario: Server-side refusal is surfaced honestly
  Given the client believes the gate is open but the server disagrees
  When the enable request returns 422 gate_evidence_required
  Then the outstanding item keys from the response are rendered inline and the toggle returns to disabled

Scenario: Emergency re-disable
  Given live trading is enabled
  When the owner disables it and confirms
  Then the confirmation copy states that new live orders stop and existing positions remain manageable in reduce-only mode
  And the change propagates to all sessions within 2 seconds

Scenario: A non-owner cannot see or act
  Given a manager opens /admin/flags
  Then the trading.live_enabled row is absent or read-only per RBAC, and no enable affordance is rendered
```

Re-sized **5 -> 3** during the DoR sizing review. Data: `GET /api/v1/admin/security/summary` (gate + key-audit results), `GET /api/v1/admin/feature-flags`, `PUT /api/v1/admin/feature-flags/{flagKey}` with `{value, reason, evidence_url}`, `POST /api/v1/auth/step-up` for the elevated token. title: Harden the Demo to Live switch on SCR-074 with gate, step-up and disarm
body:
## Context
Implements the **live half of US-PAPER-002 Explicit Demo↔Live switching** (Must). E38 shipped the switcher for demo; E44 hardens the path *into* live so that, per the story, "switching to Live requires typing a confirmation phrase and passing step-up authentication, and one-click trading is disarmed on switch", and "no hotkey can change the environment; it requires a deliberate click".

Screen **SCR-074** (Environment switcher) already specifies the transition contract: the client tears down and re-establishes every private subscription, order entry is blocked for the whole transition (typically ≤2 s), and a half-switched state is never reachable.

## Scope / Deliverables
- The LIVE path of SCR-074: typed confirmation (`ConfirmDialog variant="typed"`, must type `LIVE`) + 2FA/step-up, the list of working demo orders with the statement that they stay on demo and are not migrated, and the Live accounts available list.
- **New gate-closed state**: when `trading.live_enabled` is OFF, the switch to LIVE is unavailable with the reason and a link to SCR-137 for owners (non-owners see the plain refusal, not the gate internals).
- **Not-permitted state**: "The owner hasn't enabled Live for your account." driven by `allowed_environments` from `GET /auth/session` / WS `auth_ok` (US-PAPER-007).
- **Transition orchestration**: close private subscriptions → call `POST /api/v1/session/environment` with the step-up token → re-authenticate the WS → resubscribe; order entry disabled for the whole transition with the progress states drawn in the design; failure returns to the previous environment with the reason and no partial state.
- **One-click disarm on switch**: CMP-229 ArmToggle is forced to disarmed on any environment change, and cannot be re-armed within the transition.
- **Hotkey prohibition**: a test asserts the switch action is not registered in the hotkey map and cannot be triggered by any key binding (SCR-074: "deliberately not bindable to a hotkey; the control is click-only").
- Post-switch: a full-width confirmation banner for 10 s; the chrome and all badges re-render together (E44-S03 owns the badges themselves).

## Out of scope
- The demo-direction switch (E38, already shipped) beyond regression coverage.
- The badge/chrome visual language (E44-S03).
- Backend environment switching, the guard and the flag (E44-T03/T04).
- Blocking the switch while an algo or trade group is running is drawn in design and enforced here as a client-side precondition; the authoritative server refusal lives in E44-T03.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Switching to live requires typed confirmation and step-up
  Given the gate is open and the user is permitted live
  When the user opens SCR-074 and selects LIVE
  Then the switch button stays disabled until the exact word LIVE is typed and a valid 2FA code is supplied
  And on success POST /api/v1/session/environment is called with the step-up token

Scenario: One-click is disarmed by the switch
  Given one-click trading is armed in demo
  When the environment switches to live
  Then one-click is disarmed, and the arm control cannot be re-armed until the transition completes

Scenario: No hotkey can switch environment
  When every registered hotkey is exercised
  Then none triggers an environment change, asserted by a test over the hotkey registry

Scenario: Gate closed blocks the switch
  Given trading.live_enabled is OFF
  Then the LIVE option is unavailable with the reason stated, and owners see a link to SCR-137

Scenario: A failed switch leaves no partial state
  Given POST /api/v1/session/environment returns 403 live_trading_disabled mid-transition
  Then the session remains in demo, private subscriptions are restored, order entry is re-enabled, and the reason is shown
  And no panel is left displaying a live badge

Scenario: Switching is blocked while an algo or trade group is running
  Given a running emulated algo
  When the user attempts to switch
  Then the switch is refused with the running items listed by name
```

## Technical notes / design
Transition is a client state machine (`idle → confirming → closing_subscriptions → authenticating → resubscribing → done|failed`) with a single owner in the session store; every trading surface reads `activeEnv` from that one store subscription so a half-switched render is impossible. The step-up token is single-scope and 5-minute lived (SCR-014); it is never persisted. On `403 step_up_required` the flow re-opens the step-up modal rather than failing outright.

## Test plan
- Unit (RTL): each transition state; typed-confirm gating; disarm-on-switch; error mapping for 403 `live_trading_disabled` / `step_up_required` / not-permitted.
- Hotkey-registry test asserting no binding maps to the switch.
- Integration: subscription teardown/resubscribe ordering against a mock WS; assert order entry is disabled throughout.
- E2E (E44-Q01): demo → live → place a confirmed live order against the demo-backed staging fixture → switch back.
- a11y: assertive announcement of the environment change; focus trap in the dialog; axe-core green.
- Coverage ≥80%.

## Security notes
Threats: an attacker-triggered environment change via CSRF or a crafted deep link (mitigated: step-up token required, POST with CSRF protection, no URL-triggered switch); a stale client continuing to act as live after a server-side revocation (mitigated: the server is authoritative on every request via E44-T03, and `system`/`auth_ok` refresh `allowed_environments`). Data classification: financial data. Security review required.

## Accessibility notes
The environment change is announced assertively; the dialog is `role="alertdialog"` with the action named in its accessible description; the typed-confirmation field has a visible label; the transition progress is a live region so a screen-reader user knows order entry is blocked; no colour-only signalling.

## Performance notes
The whole transition completes in ≤2 s p95 including teardown and resubscribe (SCR-074 performance note); order entry is blocked for the duration rather than racing.

## Observability
Audit `session.environment_switched` (high severity, server-side). Client metric `cv_ui_environment_switch_seconds` and an analytics event for abandoned switches.

- [ ] axe-core green; manual screen-reader pass recorded.
- [ ] Design QA (E44-D04) passed.

title: Ship the pervasive live-mode visual language and confirm-on-every-order default

## Context
Implements the visual-distinction scenario of **US-PAPER-002** ("a persistent accent and a text badge mark every trading-capable surface, and the badge is never colour-only"), the gated-surfaces scenario of **US-PAPER-003**, and the roadmap's E44 scope line "pervasive live-mode visual language (colour, badge, confirm-on-every-order default)".

Screens **SCR-010** (app shell chrome), **SCR-075** (Demo/Live banner & per-panel badges) and the live variant of **SCR-076** (order confirmation). `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` §0.5.1 states the invariant plainly: "Demo vs Live is never colour-only… every trading-capable surface repeats the badge locally".

## Scope / Deliverables
- **CMP-074 EnvBanner** live variant in the SCR-010 shell: text `LIVE` + icon + pattern, `role="status"`, announced on every route change, never remounted on navigation.
- **CMP-075 EnvBadgeLocal** applied to every trading-capable panel: order ticket, group ticket, DOM ladder, positions grid, algo monitor, chart trading overlay, and repeated in floating windows; every such panel's accessible name includes the environment ("Order ticket - LIVE - Main").
- **CMP-139 EnvironmentAwareOrderGuard** wired around the order ticket and DOM click-to-trade handlers as client-side defence in depth: a mismatch renders the control disabled-with-reason (never silently rerouted), matching the server refusal from E44-T03.
- **Confirm-on-every-order in live**: `confirm_market_orders` and the order-confirmation modal default ON in live; "don't ask again" is available in demo only and absent in live (SCR-076 design checklist); the confirmation copy restates the environment ("You are about to send a **LIVE** order").
- **Gated surfaces**: order ticket, DOM click-to-trade, chart trading, positions actions and rule arming all reflect the current environment and refuse cross-environment actions in the UI, with the reason shown.
- A **catalogue-level test** asserting that every screen listed as trading-capable renders an environment badge — the same pattern already used for CMP-227's "(estimated)" contract.

## Out of scope
- The switcher itself (E44-S02) and the gate UI (E44-S01).
- Redesigning the order ticket, ladder or positions grid (E30/E21/E29).
- Server-side enforcement (E44-T03) — this story is the client half and must never be the only barrier.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every trading-capable surface is badged in live
  Given the session environment is live
  When the catalogue-level badge test runs over every trading-capable screen
  Then each renders an environment badge whose accessible name contains LIVE
  And a missing badge fails the build

Scenario: The distinction survives without colour
  Given the app is rendered in greyscale and in all three colour-vision simulations
  Then DEMO and LIVE chrome remain distinguishable by text, icon and pattern

Scenario: Confirmation cannot be silenced in live
  Given the session is live
  When the order confirmation modal appears
  Then no "don't ask again" affordance is present, and the copy restates LIVE, the account and the full order

Scenario: A mismatched order is blocked client-side with a reason
  Given the active environment is demo and a control targets a live account
  Then CMP-139 renders the control disabled with the reason stated, and no request is sent

Scenario: The banner is never lost
  Given the user navigates between routes and opens a modal
  Then the banner is never scrolled away, covered by the modal, or remounted, and floating windows repeat it
```

## Technical notes / design
`activeEnv` comes from the single session store subscription established in E44-S02; `orderEnv` derives from the target account's `env` (`docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-139 data contract). The shell-level route-change announcement is implemented once in the shell, not per screen (E44-D03 handoff note). Confirmation defaults come from the trading settings block in `GET /me/settings` (`trading.confirm_market_orders`, `default_environment`) with the live override applied client-side *and* asserted server-side.

## Test plan
- Unit (RTL): banner and badge rendering per environment; CMP-139 matched/mismatched; confirmation default resolution per environment.
- Catalogue test: iterate the trading-capable screen list and assert badge presence and accessible name.
- Visual regression: CMP-074 in both states at every theme (mandated by `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-074 tests), plus greyscale exports.
- Integration: CMP-139 attempts a live order while env=demo and asserts a hard block plus the audit entry (the component's mandated test).
- a11y: axe-core across the shell and each badged panel; manual screen-reader pass verifying the badge is announced on route change without being re-announced on every panel re-render (CMP-075 contract).
- Coverage ≥80%.

## Security notes
This is a safety control, not decoration: suppressing or failing to render a badge is a `priority/p0-critical` defect. Threats: a user misreading the environment and submitting a live order believing it was demo (mitigated: text+icon+pattern, per-panel repetition, mandatory confirmation); client-side-only guarding being trusted (mitigated: E44-T03 is authoritative and the mismatch test asserts the server also refuses). Security review required.

## Accessibility notes
Text always rendered, never icon/colour alone; `role="status"` for the banner and `role="img"` with a static label for the local badge so it is not re-announced on every re-render; contrast ≥4.5:1 in both themes; the distinction is verified in greyscale.

## Performance notes
The band is part of the app shell and never remounts on route change; badge state comes from one shared store subscription (SCR-075 performance note). Adding the badges must not regress panel render time measurably (<1 ms per panel).

## Observability
No analytics of its own (SCR-075 is presentational); the environment value is included in every trading audit record server-side. Add a client-side assertion metric `cv_ui_missing_env_badge_total` that should always be zero and alerts if it ever increments.

- [ ] Visual-regression baselines for CMP-074/075 in both states and themes.
- [ ] axe-core green; manual screen-reader pass recorded.
- [ ] Design QA (E44-D04) passed; Storybook entries updated.

title: Implement per-manager live eligibility with audited grant and revocation
body:
## Context
Implements **US-PAPER-007 Demo eligibility per manager** (Should). Its NFR is the design constraint: "eligibility is a server-side attribute of the user-account binding" — not a client preference, not a role. This is what lets a new manager start demo-only and be promoted deliberately, and what makes revocation safe for someone holding open live positions.

Screens: **SCR-122** Admin: user detail / edit (the owner's control) and **SCR-074** (the manager's experience of the restriction, already stubbed in E44-S02's not-permitted state).

## Scope / Deliverables
- Backend: a `live_enabled` attribute on the user↔account binding (the binding model from US-ADMIN-002, `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §14 account scope), default OFF for every new binding; migration included. It feeds `allowed_environments` on `GET /auth/session` and the WS `auth_ok` frame, and is one of the facts the E44-T03 guard checks.
- Owner UI on SCR-122: grant/revoke live per binding, step-up gated, with the audited grant recorded (actor, target user, account, before/after).
- **Acknowledgement at next sign-in**: when live access is granted, the manager must acknowledge the change at their next sign-in before live becomes selectable; the acknowledgement is recorded with its timestamp.
- **Revocation with open positions**: revoking while the manager holds live positions must not force-close anything — new entries are refused while reduce-only actions remain available, and both the owner and the manager are informed (mirrors the US-ADMIN-003 tighten-during-open-position pattern).
- Manager-side rendering: the Live switch is disabled with the reason shown (not silently absent), and no live account is selectable.

## Out of scope
- Roles, bindings CRUD and the rest of SCR-122 (E42 / US-ADMIN-002).
- Risk caps (E39 / US-ADMIN-003).
- The global gate — a grant is meaningless while `trading.live_enabled` is OFF, and the UI must say so.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A new binding is demo-only by default
  When the owner binds a manager to a sub-account
  Then live_enabled is false, no live account is selectable for that manager, and the Live switch is disabled with the reason shown

Scenario: Promotion requires acknowledgement
  Given the owner grants live access with step-up
  Then the grant is audited with before/after
  And at the manager's next sign-in they must acknowledge the change before live becomes selectable, and the acknowledgement is recorded

Scenario: Revocation with open live positions
  Given a manager holds an open live position
  When the owner revokes live access
  Then no position is force-closed
  And new live entries are refused with a stated reason while reduce-only actions still succeed
  And both the owner and the manager are informed

Scenario: The grant cannot be forged client-side
  Given a manager tampers with the client to select a live account
  When any trading request is made
  Then the server refuses with 403 and the attempt is audited as high severity

Scenario: Grant is inert while the global gate is closed
  Given trading.live_enabled is OFF
  Then a granted manager still cannot switch to live, and the UI states that the deployment-level gate is closed rather than blaming their permissions
```

## Technical notes / design
No new permission is introduced (`docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §14 explicitly rejects splitting live into its own permission); `live_enabled` is an attribute of the binding consumed by the existing environment leg of the 4-tuple. `allowed_environments` = deployment `environment_allowlist` ∩ per-binding eligibility ∩ flag state, computed server-side only. Reduce-only enforcement reuses the OMS intent classification from E29.

## Test plan
- Unit: eligibility resolution truth table (allowlist × binding × flag); acknowledgement state machine.
- Contract: `allowed_environments` identical between `GET /auth/session` and WS `auth_ok`.
- Integration: grant → acknowledge → switch; revoke-with-open-position → reduce-only still permitted, entry refused; tampered client refused and audited.
- E2E (E44-Q01): owner grants, manager acknowledges and switches.
- a11y: axe-core on SCR-122 control and the disabled-with-reason state.
- Coverage ≥90% backend, ≥80% frontend.

## Security notes
Threats: elevation of privilege (a manager granting themselves live — mitigated: owner-only + step-up + audit); repudiation of a grant (mitigated: audited with before/after and actor); a revoked manager continuing to trade on a cached session (mitigated: eligibility is re-evaluated server-side per request and pushed on the `system` topic). Data classification: financial data + access control. Security review required.

## Accessibility notes
The disabled Live switch exposes its reason via `aria-describedby`; the acknowledgement dialog is `role="alertdialog"` with the change stated in plain language; the grant/revoke controls are labelled with the target user and account, not just "on/off".

## Performance notes
Eligibility resolution is in-memory on the request path; ≤0.5 ms p95, inside the ≤5 ms total risk-check budget.

## Observability
Audit: a grant/revoke event with before/after (reusing the `user.role_assigned`-class vocabulary extended for bindings), plus the acknowledgement. Metric `cv_live_eligible_bindings` gauge.
